description: Rules for resolving conflicting claims. Versioned and published so that any consumer can reproduce a resolution and audit why one value won. Every resolved conflict records the deciding policy version in resolved_by, so a later policy change does not silently rewrite the reasoning behind data already published.

precedence.applies_when: The source is a verified official account AND the claim concerns identifiers or episode numbering WITHIN that source's own namespace.
precedence.requires: Verification of the claiming organisation. An unverified claim of officiality carries no precedence at all, because otherwise forging one is the cheapest way to poison the graph.
precedence.note: Authority is namespace-scoped. A streaming platform is authoritative about its own catalogue identifiers and its own episode numbering. It is not authoritative about which MyAnimeList entry corresponds, because that is a claim about somebody else's database. Outside its own namespace an official source ranks as ordinary evidence.

precedence.applies_when: A person opened both sources, checked, and recorded the observed source and retrieval date alongside themselves.
Two sources whose derivation roots are provably disjoint agree.
precedence.note: Computed against the declared derivation graph, never asserted. Fails closed when a source's lineage is undeclared, because treating an unknown source as independent is how two copies of one upstream become false agreement.

precedence.applies_when: No higher rule applies. The more recent assertion wins.
precedence.note: Rank alone is not sufficient. A stale official assertion does not outrank a current verified correction; see the appeal rule below.

rules.note_on_retention: Losing claims stay in conflicts[]. Overwriting without a record removes the ability to notice that a source is systematically wrong.
rules.note_on_disputes: Publish both, rank neither. A disputed pair is exempt from the one-exact-mapping-per-namespace rule, because the disagreement is the fact being recorded.
rules.appeal: A human-verified correction may outrank a stale assertion from an authoritative source. The disagreement is recorded, never erased.
rules.note_on_rollback: Where a contributor is found to have submitted systematically wrong data, their assertions can be identified and reverted as a set.

publication.note_on_declaration: Every artifact declares which evidence classes it carries and contains nothing outside that declaration. An artifact that quietly includes a class it does not declare is worse than one that excludes it, because a consumer cannot tell.
publication.note_on_vendoring: Consumers vendor a copy rather than calling a service, so corrections cannot be pushed and precision at publication time matters more than it would for a hosted dataset. Known-bad assertions are withdrawn by identifier through the revocation feed.

evidence_class_ordering.note: These are categories of backing, not a ranked scale. Consumers must not treat asserted, verified and corroborated as a ladder. Precedence between conflicting claims is decided by the precedence rules above, which consider the claim and its scope, not by sorting the class names.
